items.reason: Source: "There are men from whom warm words are small indignity." The words come FROM such men (Ahab excusing his own heat); the candidate's "men for whom hot words are no real offense" shifts it to the hearer.
items.new: "Listen again — the deeper layer. All visible things, man, are nothing but cardboard masks. But in each event — in the living act, the undeniable deed — there, some unknown but still reasoning thing puts forth the molded shape of its features from behind the unreasoning mask. If a man would strike, strike through the mask! How can the prisoner reach outside except by thrusting through the wall? To me, the white whale is that wall, shoved close against me. Sometimes I think there's nothing beyond it. But that's enough. He tasks me. He heaps me. I see in him outrageous strength, with an inscrutable malice giving it sinew. That inscrutable thing is chiefly what I hate. And whether the white whale is the agent or the principal, I will wreak that hate upon him. Don't talk to me of blasphemy, man — I'd strike the sun if it insulted me. For if the sun could do that, then I could do the other, since there is always a kind of fair play in this, with jealousy presiding over all creation. But not even that fair play is my master, man. Who is over me? Truth knows no boundaries. Take your eyes off me! More unbearable than a fiend's glare is a dull, stupid stare! So, so — you flush red and go pale. My heat has melted you into an angry glow. But listen, Starbuck — what is said in heat unsays itself. There are men from whom hot words are only a small indignity. I didn't mean to provoke you. Let it go. Look! See those Turkish cheeks of spotted tawny brown — living, breathing pictures painted by the sun. The pagan leopards — the heedless, unworshipping things that live and seek and give no reasons for the torrid life they feel! The crew, man, the crew! Aren't they one and all with Ahab in this matter of the whale? See Stubb — he laughs! See that Chilean — he snorts just thinking of it. Stand up against the general hurricane? Your one tossed sapling cannot, Starbuck! And what is it? Think about it. It's only helping to strike a fin — no great feat for Starbuck. What more is it? From this one poor hunt, then, the best lance out of all Nantucket will surely not hang back, when every common sailor has already grabbed a whetstone? Ah! I can see it seizing you — the wave lifts you! Speak — speak! Yes, yes! Your silence, then — that speaks for you. (Aside) Something shot from my flaring nostrils, and he has breathed it into his lungs. Starbuck is mine now. He cannot oppose me now without rebellion."

items.reason: Source: "the hollow flap of the sails against the masts, as for a moment their hearts sank in" — the sails' bellies actually sank in; "as if" turns the event into a simile.
items.new: But in his joy at the mate's enchanted, silent consent, Ahab did not hear his ominous prayer. Nor the low laugh from the hold. Nor the foreboding vibrations of the wind in the rigging. Nor the hollow flap of the sails against the masts, as for a moment their hearts sank in. For again Starbuck's downcast eyes lit up with the stubbornness of life. The subterranean laugh died away. The winds blew on. The sails filled out. The ship heaved and rolled as before. Ah, you warnings and omens! Why don't you stay when you come? But rather than warnings, you are predictions — you shadows! Yet not so much predictions from outside as confirmations of what was already inside. For with little to restrain us from without, the deepest necessities within our being still drive us on.

items.reason: Source: "That wild madness that's only calm to comprehend itself!" — its only calm is in comprehending itself; "only calm enough to" implies a limited degree of calm.
items.new: It was not so hard a task. I expected to find at least one man stubborn, but my one geared circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve. Or, if you prefer, like so many anthills of gunpowder, they all stand before me — and I am their match. Oh, how hard! That to set others ablaze, the match itself must burn away! What I have dared, I have willed. And what I have willed, I will do! They think me mad — Starbuck does. But I am demonic. I am madness maddened! That wild madness that is calm only to comprehend itself! The prophecy said I would be dismembered — and yes! I lost this leg. I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer. So let the prophet and the fulfiller be one. That's more than you great gods ever were. I laugh at you and hoot at you, you cricket-players, you boxers, you deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes! I will not say as schoolboys say to bullies: pick on someone your own size, don't pummel me! No — you've knocked me down, and I am up again. But you have run and hidden. Come out from behind your cotton bags! I have no long gun to reach you. Come, Ahab sends his compliments — come and see if you can swerve me. Swerve me? You cannot swerve me — or else you swerve yourselves! There, man has you. Swerve me? The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, and my soul is grooved to run on them. Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under the beds of torrents, I rush unerringly! Nothing is an obstacle, nothing is an angle on the iron way!

items.new: MALTESE SAILOR. (Reclining and shaking his cap.) It's the waves — the whitecaps are dancing now. They'll shake their tassels soon. If only all the waves were women — then I'd gladly go drown, and dance with them forever! There's nothing so sweet on earth — heaven itself can't match it — as those swift glances from warm, wild women's bosoms in the dance, when their arching arms hide such ripe, bursting grapes.

items.reason: Source (a crux): "It was hardly to be doubted, that several vessels reported to have encountered ... a Sperm Whale of uncommon magnitude and malignity ... to some minds it was not an unfair presumption, I say, that the whale in question must have been no other than Moby Dick." The certainty attaches to the identification with Moby Dick, not to the existence of the reports; the candidate moves "hardly any doubt" onto "ships had reported".
items.new: For some time past, though only at intervals, the solitary, secluded White Whale had haunted those uncivilized seas mostly visited by the sperm whale hunters. But not all of them knew of his existence. Only a few, comparatively, had knowingly seen him, and the number who had actually and knowingly fought him was very small indeed. For many reasons — the large number of whale ships; the disorderly way they were scattered over the entire watery globe, many of them adventurously pushing their hunt along lonely latitudes, so that for a whole year or more at a stretch they might seldom or never meet a single sail of any sort that could tell them news; the extreme length of each voyage; the irregular times of sailing from home — all these, with other circumstances direct and indirect, had long prevented the specific news about Moby Dick as an individual from spreading through the whole worldwide whaling fleet. Several ships were reported to have encountered, at such and such a time or on such and such a meridian, a sperm whale of unusual size and malignity which, after doing great damage to its attackers, had completely escaped them; it could hardly be doubted — to some minds, I say, it was not an unfair assumption — that this whale must have been none other than Moby Dick. Yet since the sperm whale fishery had lately seen various and not infrequent instances of great ferocity, cunning, and malice in the whale under attack, those who by accident unknowingly fought Moby Dick were perhaps, for the most part, content to blame the peculiar terror he inspired more, as it were, on the dangers of the sperm whale fishery at large than on the individual cause. That, mostly, was how the disastrous encounter between Ahab and the whale had so far been popularly regarded.

items.reason: Source: "broken limbs, or devouring amputations" — "devouring" (the limb taken by the jaw) became the generic "horrific".
items.new: As for those who had previously heard of the White Whale and then happened to see him — at first, almost every one of them had lowered for him as boldly and fearlessly as for any other sperm whale. But eventually, such catastrophes resulted from these attacks — not just sprained wrists and ankles, broken limbs, or devouring amputations, but fatalities of the deadliest kind — that these repeated, disastrous defeats, all piling their terrors onto Moby Dick, had gone far toward shaking the courage of many brave hunters who eventually heard the story of the White Whale.

items.new: Nevertheless, some there were who, even knowing all this, were ready to chase Moby Dick. And an even greater number, having only heard of him vaguely and at a distance, without specific details of any particular disaster and without the superstitious trappings, were tough enough not to flee from the fight if it came to them.

items.reason: Source: "Ahab had some glimpse of this, namely: all my means are sane, my motive and my object mad." Melville gives Ahab's self-knowledge in the first person; the candidate turns this famous line into reported third-person speech.
items.new: Now, in his heart, Ahab had some glimpse of this — namely: all my means are sane, my motive and my object mad. Yet without power to kill, change, or escape the fact, he also knew that he had long been deceiving mankind about it — and in some ways still was. But his deception was only subject to his awareness, not to his deliberate will. Nevertheless, he succeeded so well in it that when he stepped ashore on his ivory leg at last, no Nantucketer thought him anything other than naturally grief-stricken, and deeply so, by the terrible accident that had befallen him.

items.reason: Source: "more strangely hideous than the ugliest abortion." Period sense is a monstrous, misshapen birth. "Birth defect" is a modern clinical softening (a condition, not a creature) and is inconsistent with 55.9, which keeps "authentic abortions" with a gloss. Answer to the open question: keep the period term with a brief gloss (lead decision 1; hard rule 4).
items.new: What is it about the albino man that so particularly repels and often shocks the eye, so that he is sometimes despised by his own family? It is the whiteness that covers him, the very thing expressed by his name. The albino is as well-built as other men — he has no real deformity — and yet this all-pervading whiteness makes him more strangely hideous than the ugliest abortion (a misshapen, monstrous birth). Why should this be?
